patterns.heading: Spawn point versus block coordinate
patterns.question: Does a coordinate represent an entity/player position or a block/region coordinate?
patterns.negativeControl: Fractional authored coordinates can already be exact intended positions; block operations do not require centering
patterns.prohibits: Never adjust map coordinates or claim a spatial bug based on an unconditional +0.5 rule

patterns.heading: Damage: JSON or script?
patterns.question: Is damage controlled by the entity's own JSON state, or by game/arena/team phase conditions in script?
candidateRelations: entity component or component-group → local damage policy
round/arena/team state guard → conditional damage treatment
patterns.negativeControl: An entity with a static damage sensor may correctly implement its full behavior without a Script API handler
patterns.prohibits: Do not assume invulnerability, friendly-fire policy or required script handlers from component names alone, or equate authored sensor with live damage prevention

patterns.heading: Removing entities: choose by intent
patterns.question: Is entity disappearance part of a combat outcome or a reset/cleanup lifecycle?
patterns.negativeControl: A kill used for intentional combat outcome and a removal used for cleanup can both be valid
patterns.prohibits: Never equate remove/despawn with a win, or require one removal method for all maps

patterns.heading: Form service and force-close rules
patterns.question: Does this map tie a pending form response to the same session/phase that opened it?
patterns.negativeControl: A legitimately persistent, non-session-specific form is not automatically stale
patterns.prohibits: Do not classify an unguarded form as a bug without selected-map design and reachable effect evidence

patterns.heading: Action bar ownership
patterns.question: What gameplay state does the HUD describe, and what happens to time-limited feedback on round transitions, death or lobby return?
candidateRelations: phase / round state → candidate player-facing HUD text
temporary feedback → possible expiration or replacement
patterns.negativeControl: A command-driven HUD or multiple independently scoped display owners may be intentional and correct in a particular map
patterns.prohibits: Do not require a single HUD adapter or diagnose a stale HUD from source calls without verifying player-visible output and approved behavior

patterns.heading: Console and logging boundaries
patterns.question: Is the message intended for players or for developer diagnosis, and is it on a material gameplay path?
patterns.negativeControl: Intentional player-facing diagnostic information or admin tools can be part of approved map design
patterns.prohibits: Do not issue a defect merely for nonconformity with this team's preferred logger

patterns.heading: Data places and world versus player storage
patterns.question: Which actor/session/arena owns the state, how long does it survive, and where is the reset or recovery?
patterns.negativeControl: Scoreboards can legitimately store gameplay state in maps; the author's display-only preference is not universal
patterns.prohibits: Do not mark scoreboard storage or a different persistence strategy as defective merely for differing from this author's preference

patterns.heading: Profiling
patterns.question: Which potentially high-frequency source operations have a measured effect on active gameplay, and what phase/concurrency context is relevant?
candidateRelations: entity query / chunk check → candidate active-phase runtime work
patterns.negativeControl: High call frequency alone does not prove lag or a performance bug; performance depends on actual target device, concurrency and measured timings
patterns.prohibits: Do not report runtime lag from a static hot-spot signature, copy the author's performance percentages, or assume a 30-player target applies to other maps

patterns.heading: Playing sounds from script
patterns.question: Is the sound event a feedback cue, an ambient loop, or part of an authored gameplay sequence, and which player/group is its intended audience?
candidateRelations: event or action → attempted audible cue
patterns.negativeControl: An intentional music or sound cue may not correspond to a terminal win/lose action; no sound is required by default
patterns.prohibits: Do not treat an authored sound reference as delivered audio, a win condition, or evidence that an event succeeded

patterns.heading: Soft teleport sequence
patterns.question: Does moving between gameplay stages intentionally close UI, apply camera feedback and preserve player control?
patterns.negativeControl: An immediate teleport without fade can be valid if selected-map design expects it
patterns.prohibits: Do not require soft teleport universally or classify bare teleport as a bug without evidence

patterns.heading: Sending text: Script API first
patterns.question: Which player-facing objective or state is communicated through localized text, item/entity name tags or custom glyphs, and is that information actually reachable?
candidateRelations: translation key → possible player-facing authored instruction
nameTag or custom glyph → candidate presentation context
UI text → interpretation cue, not standalone rule
patterns.negativeControl: Unicode or command-based messages may be deliberately supported by the target resource pack/client; missing visible text cannot be inferred from one author's ASCII-only rule
patterns.prohibits: Do not turn developer text-style preferences into game rules or infer a completed objective merely from a success message translation key

patterns.heading: Gameplay time and exception for recording
patterns.question: What is the intended time authority for cooldowns, round progression and session expiry?
patterns.negativeControl: Wall-clock timestamps may be intentional telemetry or an approved design requirement
patterns.prohibits: Do not infer a time bug solely from Date.now or silently require 20 TPS as a runtime observation

patterns.heading: Inspect targets and upgrade together
patterns.question: Are claimed Script API capabilities applicable to this selected archive's manifest and target edition/version?
patterns.negativeControl: A pin mismatch requires verification of actual dependency and runtime target, not assumptions from filenames
patterns.prohibits: Do not use a version pinned in this developer ZIP as the selected map's runtime profile

patterns.heading: The rule: chunks load around the player, so move the player to the scene
patterns.question: When a selected map attempts a scene-camera relocation, does it explicitly account for player-centered loaded/chunk-visible space and later restore player state?
candidateRelations: teleport attempt → possible visual load boundary
patterns.negativeControl: An in-range camera or intentionally distant noninteractive view can be correct; a teleport site by itself neither proves camera usage nor that rendering failed.
patterns.prohibits: Never infer sky-only rendering or force a behind-camera teleport for an unrelated map from a teleport cue; require selected-source camera linkage and scoped visual proof.

patterns.heading: Decide
patterns.question: Is the observed dynamic-property read/write backed by the selected map's own state ownership, or is static JSON configuration being confused with mutable runtime state?
candidateRelations: saved runtime state → reload/rejoin lifecycle candidate
patterns.negativeControl: Dynamic properties may intentionally coexist with JSON components, scoreboard displays or temporary state; a reference project's architecture is not this map's game design.
patterns.prohibits: Never reclassify a world or player state store as a bug merely because it differs from the reference team's JSON-versus-script convention.

patterns.heading: Setup that can run any number of times
patterns.question: Does an observed recurring callback repeat an irreversible effect or spawn instead of reconciling existing authored objects, and what call/state guard governs the path?
patterns.negativeControl: A periodic callback or repeated update can be intentional, bounded, and efficient; the source pattern's T17 observations do not establish measured lag in another map.
patterns.prohibits: Never classify an interval as a performance bug or claim duplicate entities without inspecting the selected map's guard, current object identity, and proof.
